fanoutqa_014361.x:
Paris :: History :: 20th and 21st centuries :: part 03 :: chunk_0010
In 2007, President [Nicolas Sarkozy](/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy") launched the [Grand Paris](/wiki/Grand_Paris "Grand Paris") project to integrate Paris more closely with the towns in the region around it. After many modifications, the new area, named the [Metropolis of Grand Paris](/wiki/Grand_Paris "Grand Paris"), with a population of 6.7 million, was created on 1 January 2016.[[78]](#cite_note-Lichfield-80) The City of Paris and the national government approved the plans for the [Grand Paris Express](/wiki/Grand_Paris_Express "Grand Paris Express") four years later, totalling 205 km (127 mi) of automated metro lines to connect Paris, the innermost three departments around Paris, airports and [high-speed rail (TGV)](/wiki/TGV "TGV") stations, at an estimated cost of €35 billion.[[79]](#cite_note-metro-81) The system is scheduled to be completed by 2030.[[80]](#cite_note-82)

A [series of attacks](/wiki/January_2015_%C3%8Ele-de-France_attacks "January 2015 Île-de-France attacks") occurred in the Paris region, especially in Paris, in January 2015, the most serious being the [shooting at the offices](/wiki/Charlie_Hebdo_shooting "Charlie Hebdo shooting") of [Charlie Hebdo](/wiki/Charlie_Hebdo "Charlie Hebdo"). 17 people died in the attacks, which [Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula](/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_the_Arabian_Peninsula "Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula") claimed responsibility.[[81]](#cite_note-83)[[82]](#cite_note-84) [1.5 million people marched in Paris](/wiki/Republican_marches "Republican marches") in a show of solidarity against terrorism and in support of freedom of speech.[[83]](#cite_note-85) [Terrorist attacks](/wiki/November_2015_Paris_attacks "November 2015 Paris attacks"), claimed by ISIL,[[84]](#cite_note-86) occurred again in November, which killed 130 people and injured more than 350.[[85]](#cite_note-87)

In *[Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince](/wiki/Harry_Potter_and_the_Half-Blood_Prince "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince")* (2005), Dumbledore brings Harry along as he attempts to persuade [Horace Slughorn](/wiki/Horace_Slughorn "Horace Slughorn") to rejoin the Hogwarts faculty as the Potions professor. Harry excels in Slughorn's class after he begins using an old textbook that once belonged to someone known as "The Half-Blood Prince". Outside of class, Dumbledore uses the [Pensieve](/wiki/Pensieve "Pensieve") to teach Harry about Voldemort's life and his rise to power. Harry and Dumbledore learn that Voldemort created six [Horcruxes](/wiki/Horcrux "Horcrux") to gain immortality, and that they must be destroyed before Voldemort can be killed. Harry repeatedly warns Dumbledore that Draco Malfoy is an agent of Voldemort, but Dumbledore refuses to take action against Draco. He tells Harry that he already knows more about what is happening than Harry does. During the course of the novel, Harry becomes romantically involved with Ginny.

Near the end of the book, Dumbledore and Harry enter a cave in search of a Horcrux. Dumbledore drinks a potion inside the Horcrux's container and begins to scream in agony. When Harry attempts to retrieve some lake water for Dumbledore to drink, he is attacked by [Inferi](/wiki/Inferius "Inferius"). They try to drown Harry, but Dumbledore rescues him. Dumbledore and Harry then return to the Hogwarts [Astronomy Tower](/wiki/Magic_in_Harry_Potter#Astronomy "Magic in Harry Potter") with the Horcrux. Dumbledore asks Harry not to interfere in the events that are about to take place, and puts him in a body-binding curse. Immobilized, Harry is unable to intervene as Snape arrives and kills Dumbledore. Later, Harry ends his relationship with Ginny to protect her from Voldemort.

The east facade in March 2021

The Parthenon is an [octastyle](/wiki/Octastyle "Octastyle") [peripteral](/wiki/Peripteral "Peripteral") [Doric](/wiki/Doric_order "Doric order") temple with an [Ionic](/wiki/Ionic_order "Ionic order") [hexastyle](/wiki/Hexastyle "Hexastyle") [amphiprostyle](/wiki/Amphiprostyle "Amphiprostyle") two-chambered [cella](/wiki/Cella "Cella"). It was built on the [euthynteria](/wiki/Euthynteria "Euthynteria") and [krepis](/wiki/Crepidoma "Crepidoma") of its precursor building, the [Older Parthenon](/wiki/Older_Parthenon "Older Parthenon"). In common with other Greek temples, the Parthenon is built using the [post and lintel](/wiki/Post_and_lintel "Post and lintel") construction, surrounded by columns ('peripteral') carrying an [entablature](/wiki/Entablature "Entablature"). The gable-end of the Parthenon features eight columns instead of the traditional six found in typical Doric temples. Although octastyle temples were not entirely unknown, their presence in mainland Doric architecture, along with the wider inner masonry structure, the *[cella](/wiki/Cella "Cella")*,[[64]](#cite_note-64) makes the Parthenon unique in its design.[[note 1]](#cite_note-67) There are seventeen columns on the sides. A ratio of 4:9 proportion is found in the elevation and the relationship of the columns to their spacing (the interaxial). There is a double row of columns at both the front and rear. In 1802, Napoleon created the [lycée](/wiki/Secondary_education_in_France "Secondary education in France"), the second and final stage of secondary education that prepares students for higher education studies or a profession.[[292]](#cite_note-304) [Jules Ferry](/wiki/Jules_Ferry "Jules Ferry") is considered the father of the French modern school, leading reforms in the late 19th century that established free, secular and compulsory education (currently mandatory to age 16).[[293]](#cite_note-305)[[294]](#cite_note-306)

French education is centralised and divided into three stages: primary, secondary, and higher education. The [Programme for International Student Assessment](/wiki/Programme_for_International_Student_Assessment "Programme for International Student Assessment"), coordinated by the OECD, ranked France's education as near the OECD average in 2018.[[295]](#cite_note-307)[[296]](#cite_note-oecd-308) School children in France reported greater concern about the disciplinary climate and behaviour in classrooms compared to other OECD countries.[[296]](#cite_note-oecd-308)
